app.name: Suraksha
app.tagline: Check a suspicious message before you trust it

footer.disclaimer: Suraksha is a safety assistant, not a guarantee. If you are unsure, call your bank's official number — from your passbook or your branch — never a number from the message.

home.heading: Got a suspicious message?
home.subheading: Paste it here. Suraksha will tell you if it is a scam — and why.
home.placeholder: Paste the SMS, WhatsApp message or link here…
home.emptyError: Paste or type a message first.

check.noReasons: No known scam signals were found. Stay careful — a clean check is not a guarantee.
check.overrideNote: One signal here is dangerous on its own, so the verdict is raised regardless of the rest.
check.emptyState: No message to check. Go back and paste one.

ai.downloading: Downloading the AI model once — after this it works offline.

verdictLine.safe: No scam signals found — but always stay alert.
verdictLine.caution: Some warning signs. Do not act in a hurry; verify first.
verdictLine.risky: Several scam signs. Treat this as a scam until you have verified it.
verdictLine.danger: This is a scam. Do not share any code, do not pay, do not install anything.

credential.secretAsk: It asks for your OTP, PIN or password. No bank, wallet or official ever asks for these — anyone who does is stealing.
credential.remoteAccess: It mentions a screen-sharing app like AnyDesk or TeamViewer. Scammers use these to watch your phone and empty your account.
credential.installApp: It tells you to install an app or switch on special permissions. This is how scammers take control of phones.

upi.collectToReceive: It says entering your UPI PIN or approving a request will bring you money. Your PIN only ever sends money OUT — receiving needs nothing.
upi.qrReceive: It asks you to scan a QR code to receive money. Receiving money never needs a QR scan.
upi.wrongTransferReturn: It claims money reached you by mistake and asks you to send it back. This is a known trap — check your own bank app, then talk to your branch.
upi.refundBait: It dangles a refund or cashback out of nowhere. Fake refunds are used to make you approve payments.
upi.unusualVpa: The UPI ID uses an uncommon provider. Check the receiver's name in your UPI app before paying anything.

url.apkDownload: It links to an app file (APK/EXE) download. Apps from links can watch your screen and empty your account — install only from the Play Store.
url.lookalikeDomain: The website address imitates a real bank or service, but it is not the official address.
url.punycodeHomoglyph: The link uses look-alike characters to disguise a fake website address.
url.shortener: The link is shortened, hiding where it really leads. Banks and offices do not send shortened links.
url.ipAddress: The link points to a raw number address instead of a real website name. No bank does this.
url.suspiciousTld: The website ends in a cheap domain that fraudsters commonly use.
url.httpBank: A link about banking is not using a secure (https) address. Real bank sites are always secure.
url.govClaimNonGov: It talks about a government scheme, but the link is not a government (.gov.in) website.
url.excessiveSubdomains: The web address is stretched with many extra parts to look official. Genuine addresses are short.

loan.advanceFee: It asks for a fee, GST or deposit before giving the loan. Real lenders take charges from the loan amount — never pay money to get a loan.
loan.tooEasy: It promises a loan with no documents, no credit check or 'guaranteed' approval. Real loans always need checks; this is bait.
loan.rbiClaim: It claims to be 'RBI approved'. The RBI does not approve individual lenders — check the lender on the RBI website's NBFC list.

impersonation.authorityClaim: It claims to be from a bank, the police, RBI, income tax or a courier. Anyone can say this on a call — verify through an official number, not this message.
impersonation.digitalArrest: It threatens arrest, a warrant or a seized parcel to frighten you. This is the 'digital arrest' scam — the police never arrest or take payment over a call.
impersonation.senderIdMismatch: It claims to be your bank but gives a personal 10-digit mobile number. Real bank messages never ask you to call a personal number.

urgency.deadline: It creates a rush — 'act now', 'within hours', 'account blocked today'. This pressure is meant to stop you thinking. Slow down and verify.
urgency.secrecy: It tells you to keep this secret from family or bank staff. Honest institutions never ask for secrecy — this is how victims are cut off from help.

reward.lotteryPrize: It says you won a lottery, prize or lucky draw you never entered. Real prizes never need you to pay or share details to claim.
reward.jobUpfront: It offers easy earnings but asks for a registration or joining fee first. Real jobs pay you — they never ask you to pay to start.
reward.investment: It promises guaranteed profit or doubled money. No real investment is guaranteed; 'sure profit' offers are traps.

textual.excessiveCaps: The message is mostly in capital letters to shout and rush you. Genuine messages rarely do this.
textual.charSubstitution: Words like 'account' or 'OTP' are spelled with digits or symbols to slip past filters — a common scam trick.
textual.homoglyphWord: A word uses look-alike letters from another alphabet to disguise itself. This is deliberate trickery.
